summary: apt module options for cache validity time, apt-get clean, installing a .deb file or URL, default release pinning, dpkg options, and failing instead of removing packages.
questions: How do I only run apt-get update if the cache is older than an hour?
How do I install a local .deb file with Ansible?
Can Ansible install a .deb directly from a URL?
How do I pass dpkg force-confold options?
How do I make an apt task fail rather than remove conflicting packages?
How do I clear /var/cache/apt/archives with Ansible?

answer_card.title: apt options: cache, .deb, dpkg
answer_card.answer_md:
- `cache_valid_time` (seconds, default 0): update cache only if older; setting it implies `update_cache=yes`
- `clean`: equivalent of `apt-get clean` (runs before install)
- `deb`: path to a .deb on the remote; if it contains `://` it is downloaded first (needs `xz-utils`)
- `default_release`: like `apt -t`, sets pin priorities
- `dpkg_options` (default `force-confdef,force-confold`): comma-separated dpkg options
- `fail_on_autoremove` (no): like `--no-remove`; fail instead of removing packages
